note:
Japan is the one tradition in this table with a real national cut standard that is fetchable in full. The 牛部分肉取引規格 of 日本食肉格付協会 (JMGA) is served as HTML at https://www.jmga.or.jp/standard/beef-partial/ and its 別表1 分割・整形方法 gives, for each of the thirteen 大分割 部分肉, the exact vertebra or rib the saw crosses and — for the hindquarter — the Japanese anatomical names of the muscles whose fascia the knife follows. That makes JP the only tradition here with `standard` bounds almost everywhere. What JMGA does not do is enumerate contents: it names a muscle only when that muscle is a boundary or is called out in the trim, so most muscle lists are `trade`.

The 小分割 yakiniku vocabulary (ミスジ, ザブトン, トウガラシ, カイノミ, シンシン, イチボ, トモサンカク/ヒウチ, カメノコ, ネクタイ) has no standard at all, and is sourced here from two Japanese trade publishers: note.com/bridgeinter (高橋寛, an AUS-MEAT QA officer, who prints the 学名 in Latin beside each 小割) and toyonishifarm.co.jp, a Hokkaido producer whose 3D 部位解説 prints 主な筋肉 in Japanese veterinary nomenclature. Where a source gives the muscle only in Japanese, the Latin bridge is stated in the entry's `note` (棘下筋 = M. infraspinatus, 大腿二頭筋 = M. biceps femoris, 胸腹鋸筋 = M. serratus ventralis thoracis, and so on); the quote itself is never translated.

Two limits worth knowing before reading the bounds. First, JMGA separates かたばら from かたロース at roughly one third of the rib's length, measured *down* the rib — a cut along the ribs, not across them. `from`/`to` can only name the rib the cut crosses, so ザブトン and 三角バラ, which are both serratus ventralis over ribs 1–6, come out with identical bounds here and are told apart only by their notes. Second, the model resolves the cervical column as a single `cervical-vertebrae`, so JMGA's ネック line at 第6～第7頚椎跡間 cannot be placed exactly.

Where JMGA and the cut rectangles in cuts_jp.json disagree — and they do, on the rib numbers of リブロース and サーロイン, on whether the foreshank belongs to カタ, and on whether カメノコ is a シンタマ or a ソトモモ muscle — this file records JMGA and says so in `dispute`. cuts_jp.json is not modified.

cuts.dispute: The rib numbers here contradict cuts_jp.json, which describes リブロース as running from the fifth rib to the last rib. JMGA gives rib 7 to rib 10: the 大分割 takes まえ off at 第6～第7肋骨間 and リブロース is divided from サーロイン at 第10～第11胸椎跡間. bridgeinter confirms the same span and adds the regional split — 関西 7–10 (four ribs), 関東 6–10 (five ribs). rib-07→rib-10 follows JMGA. cuts.dispute: カルビ is not a cut in any Japanese standard — it is a menu word, borrowed from Korean 갈비, for the meat on and between the rib bones of ばら. It has no entry in JMGA's thirteen 部分肉. The muscle list here is bridgeinter's for the トモバラ small cuts he files under it. The two trade sources also mean different objects by ショートリブ: bridgeinter's is the bone-in 6–8 rib piece and he gives it serratus ventralis thoracis, while toyonishifarm's is the flat plate left after the rib fingers are cut out and gives 外腹斜筋. cuts.dispute: Graded trade for the same reason as かたばら: JMGA names 外腹斜筋 and 腹皮筋 only as trim landmarks, so the muscle list is toyonishifarm's, not the standard's. The rear bound, however, is the most interesting line in the whole Japanese standard: JMGA separates ともばら not at a bone but along the front edge of a muscle — 大腿筋膜張筋（とも三角）の前縁に沿って、寛結節（腸骨の前端）まで — so the tensor fasciae latae is the boundary and stays on the leg side. `to: ilium` is the nearest the schema can put 寛結節. The front bound is the 大分割 line at 第6～第7肋骨間, giving ribs 7–13; bridgeinter's トモバラ span of 6–12 ribs is the trade's looser reckoning and is recorded under `karubi`.

cuts.dispute: Not contested, but not unanimous either: all three sources put the internal oblique in カイノミ, two of the three add the external oblique, and toyonishifarm gives the internal oblique alone. The internal oblique is therefore `defining` and the external `major`. This agrees with the UNECE reading recorded in FINDINGS.md, where bavette d'aloyau — the same slab of meat — is the thickest portion of m. obliquus internus abdominis. Bounds are trade rather than standard: JMGA has no カイノミ, and bridgeinter places it by neighbours (behind the short plate, inside the tenderloin, anatomically past the last rib in bottom sirloin territory) rather than by a bone.

cuts.dispute: No source names a muscle for タン, and the ones consulted are explicit about it: toyonishifarm's 主な筋肉 field reads simply 舌, the tongue. bridgeinter divides the tongue by position — タン先, タン中, タン元, タン下 — and by trim spec (Swiss cut, short cut, ムキタン), never by muscle. That is not carelessness; the working vocabulary genuinely is positional, because what varies along a tongue is texture, not anatomy. The unmodelled list here is from bovine anatomy, not from a beef source, and every entry is unmodelled: the atlas's 49 muscles include no lingual muscle at all, which is the single largest gap this tradition exposes. `bone_in` is false for the Swiss cut and the ムキタン that dominate the Japanese trade; a short-cut tongue keeps the hyoid, which the model does have an id for.

The sacrocaudalis assignment is inferred from anatomy: the tail is caudal vertebrae, their sacrocaudal muscles, the intertransversarii and skin, and of those only the sacrocaudalis has an id here.
